With a strong cash position, we are well positioned to advance BGE-102 and our apelin and other programs.” Third Quarter 2026 Business Highlights BGE-102 clinical development: QUELL-DME Phase 2 trial ● In September 2026, BioAge announced that the first participant was dosed in QUELL-DME, a randomized, controlled Phase 2 trial evaluating once-daily oral BGE-102 in adults with diabetic macular edema. ● The approximately 180-participant trial evaluates BGE-102 both as monotherapy and in combination with standard-of-care anti-VEGF therapy, with participants randomized 1:1:1 across three arms. ● The primary endpoint is change from baseline in best-corrected visual acuity at week 12, and topline results are anticipated in the second half of 2027. ● Beyond DME, results from QUELL-DME will inform BioAge's development strategy in other NLRP3-driven retinal diseases, including geographic atrophy.

The trial also measures a broad set of inflammatory and cardiometabolic biomarkers. ● The trial is designed to characterize the dose-response relationship for BGE-102 and to support dose selection for further development, with topline data anticipated in the fourth quarter of 2026. ● QUELL-CV builds on the full Phase 1 dataset for BGE-102, in which the compound achieved up to 98% suppression of IL-1β at trough in an ex vivo whole-blood assay, along with median hsCRP reductions of 86% from baseline at both 60 mg and 120 mg once daily APJ agonist program advancement ● BioAge continues to advance its oral and injectable APJ agonist programs as an exercise-mimetic approach to obesity. ● Apelin, the natural ligand of APJ, is released during exercise, and APJ agonism recapitulates various metabolic benefits of exercise.
